---
title: "Weekly surveillance report"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    toc: true
lang: en-CA
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(islandbrand)
islh_setup(format = "html", quiet = TRUE)

weekly <- data.frame(
  week = seq(as.Date("2026-01-04"), by = "week", length.out = 12),
  cases = c(10, 12, 18, 29, 40, 52, 45, 31, 24, 18, 14, 10)
)
```

## Weekly pattern

Cases peak in the sixth week and then decrease. Hover over a bar for values,
drag to zoom, and double-click to reset.

```{r}
#| echo: false
islh_epi_curve(
  weekly, date = week, count = cases,
  title = "Reported cases by week",
  subtitle = "Simulated surveillance counts",
  caption = "Source: simulated example data"
) |>
  islh_plotly(height = 380)
```

## Weekly counts

Search for a week, click a column heading to sort, or move between pages.

```{r}
#| echo: false
islh_reactable(
  weekly,
  title = "Weekly counts",
  columns = list(
    week = reactable::colDef(name = "Week starting"),
    cases = reactable::colDef(name = "Reported cases")
  ),
  page_size = 5,
  source_note = "Source: simulated example data"
)
```

## Individual cases

Each tile represents one case. Hover over its area for the reporting date
and period count.

```{r}
#| echo: false
small_counts <- data.frame(
  week = as.Date("2026-01-04") + 7 * 0:1,
  cases = c(2, 1)
)
islh_epi_curve(small_counts, week, cases, style = "cases") |>
  islh_plotly(height = 280)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
grouped_counts <- data.frame(
  week = as.Date("2026-01-04"),
  cases = c(2, 1),
  area = c("North", "South")
)
islh_epi_curve(
  grouped_counts, week, cases, fill = area, facet = area, style = "cases"
) |>
  islh_plotly(height = 280)
```

## Customise an ordinary plot

Small theme changes keep the brand styling. This plot rotates its date labels
without adding a complete theme first.

```{r}
#| echo: false
plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(weekly, ggplot2::aes(week, cases)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(colour = islh_brand("primary")) +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45))
islh_plotly(plot, height = 280)
```

## Values prepared for release

This example has already had its small value replaced with a numeric missing
value. The display label keeps it distinct from an ordinary missing value,
and the remaining counts still sort numerically.

```{r}
#| echo: false
safe_counts <- data.frame(
  area = c("North", "Central", "South", "West"),
  cases = c(NA_real_, 105, 17, 42)
)
islh_reactable(
  safe_counts,
  title = "Counts prepared for release",
  columns = list(cases = reactable::colDef(na = "Suppressed"))
)
```
